reasoning.rationale: Full replica page 1 identifies EO 2976, Wilson, 16 October 1918. The operative relief suspends the eight-hour prohibition solely for construction and completion of surveying vessel PILOT; the quoted enabling proviso preserves a basic eight-hour wage rate and overtime of at least time and one-half. This is relief during construction, not an order proving that construction occurred or completed. No held completion fact or extinguishing provision establishes its first cessation. Frozen OCR materially damages the wage formula and statutory citation/date block; no bytes were corrected. No whole-case submission.
reasoning.earlier: No first-ending date is established. Completion of PILOT is a specific material factual question. Wartime purpose, the fiscal-year title of the March 4, 1917 appropriation, and elapsed age prove neither completion nor first cessation. The PLO:1557 missing-identity lead has no held provision in this dossier and is not an ending finding.
reasoning.scope: Single construction-specific suspension with immediate commencement on 1918-10-16; no general suspension for other work. Quoted statutory wage qualification must remain visible. The full page has been checked, but corrupt frozen OCR prevents confirmation of complete faithful working text.
reasoning.independent: The wage proviso qualifies the suspension; construction and completion describe its scope, not a command whose fulfillment is proved by signing. No separate reporting or contract deadline is imposed by this page.
reasoning.savings: Prospective exemption can cease while accrued wage/overtime, contract, or enforcement consequences remain. Neither their actual accrual nor extinction is established. Need enabling statute original and relevant later savings/extinguishment provisions; no blanket no-residual finding.
gaps: Actual completion of PILOT or a source first extinguishing this construction-specific suspension, with supported timing and earlier-end examination.
Original March 4, 1917 enabling act provision (39 Stat. 1192 as printed here), qualifications and any relevant later termination/savings text.
Resolve PLO:1557 lead with actual held instrument and target scope, not an absent census identity.
Materially corrupt frozen OCR: wage computation formula, statutory citation and signing-date block. Requires separately prepared faithful source representation; no silent correction.

reasoning.rationale: Full replica page 1 identifies EO 3522, Harding, July 27, 1921, amending paragraphs 40, 186 and 195 of the July 9, 1914 navigation rules. Paragraph 40 governs recurring vessel information and arrival reports with a prior-communication exception; 186 requires spark/smoke precautions and imposes damage liability; 195 requires registration/numbering or registration/certification and prohibits operation pending compliance. II supplies immediate commencement. These are continuing amended rules; an individual craft compliance event cannot terminate the general rule. Parent and subsequent provisions, first cessations and savings are not established. Frozen OCR corrupts parent year and paragraph identifiers. No whole-case submission.
reasoning.earlier: No earliest extinguishing instrument is held in this dossier. The empty named chain and zero number-search hits do not establish continued operation or a first ending. Read exact parent July 9, 1914 paragraphs 40, 186, 195 and later amendments/replacement rules with effective dates; evaluate supersession by substantive scope and savings rather than order-number silence.
reasoning.scope: Replace sole-paragraph machine inventory with amendment introduction, paragraph 40, paragraph 186, paragraph 195 and commencement II. All offsets remain in frozen OCR; visual paragraph identifiers are 40/186/195 although the OCR introduction says 40/086/j95 and parent year 194. The read-as-follows amendment is not exhaustion at signing.
reasoning.independent: Paragraph 40 retains the arrival-time report even where previous agent communication excuses other radio reporting. Paragraph 186 contains both precaution and damage-liability requirements. Paragraph 195 distinguishes powered and other private craft; its until condition governs each craft, not the continuing rule. TERM report_deadline is a misclassification of recurring navigation reporting, and TERM until_event is not a whole-order sunset.
reasoning.savings: Paragraph 186 expressly holds vessels liable for damage from neglect; no damage occurrence or outstanding liability is assumed. Paragraph 195 registration/certification may have consequences distinct from prospective rule operation. Parent and later text/savings are required to separate continuing duties, accrued liability and existing registrations. No finding that all consequences vanished.
gaps: Held exact parent July 9, 1914 navigation-rule provisions and intervening amendments, including before/after text and legal authority.
Subsequent amendments/repeals/replacement navigation and craft rules for paragraphs 40, 186 and 195; exact effective dates and specific first-cessation analysis for each independent duty.
Applicable Panama Canal Act and relevant later savings/residual provisions, particularly accrued damage liability and registration/certification effects.
Material frozen OCR corruption of parent year and amendment paragraph identifiers; separately prepare faithful source representation without changing held bytes.
